newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH NBP FLOOD CREDIT NOT TO UP BUDGET SPENDING.
newsitem.headline: POLISH NBP FLOOD CREDIT NOT TO UP BUDGET SPENDING.

text.p: The Polish government's proposed 2.5 billion zloty flood relief credit from the National Bank of Poland (NBP) will not increase total budgetary spending in 1997, Finance Minister Marek Belka said on Wednesday.

"The credit we asked the NBP to give us does not mean an increase in the total expenditures of the state, (but) it guarantess that we will not be in danger of loosing liquidity," Belka told a special paliamentary session dedicated to funding flood relief.
Belka, urging opposition to restrain calls for more relief spending, said a $300 million loan from the World Bank was the only source of funding for the flood ouside the 1997 budget.
"The flood can not serve as a pretex for us to abandon good, tested economic policies and unresponsibly spurt out unsound ideas (about funding the relief effort)," he said.
Belka also said the World bank credit would probably not be entirely consumed in 1997.

Belka said estimating losses from the flood, which claimed nearly 40 lives and put about one percent of Poland under water, was impossible because in many areas waters had not yet subsided and warned that all estimates circulating in the local media should be treated with a large degree of scepticism.
He also said regions hit by the flood would probably not pay any income taxes for the next two months, but that smaller inflows could be made up before the end of the year.
